I need to write thorough JUnit 4 tests for the TimeSeries class, covering its constructors and key methods like domain/range descriptions, item count, and maximum item count including its validation and eviction branches.

I'm continuing to map out branches for methods like maximum item age validation, data item retrieval by index or time period, index lookup with null checks, and value retrieval. The most complex area is the add methods, especially add(TimeSeriesDataItem, boolean) with its null checks, series exception for mismatched period classes, insertion logic via binary search, duplicate detection, and maximum count enforcement, plus the various overloaded add and update methods for time periods and numeric values.

Finishing createCopy's range-checking branches and moving to equals() and hashCode() branch analysis. I'm now trying to recall the specifics of the Chart-17 defect, thinking it might relate to createCopy() and shared data list references, but I'm not fully certain of the exact bug location yet.

Rather than pinpointing the exact defect, I decide to write comprehensive tests covering the TimeSeries class broadly using the Day and Year classes as concrete RegularTimePeriod implementations available in the same package. I'm sketching out a test plan covering constructors, domain/range descriptions, item counts, maximum item count/age handling, and time period class behavior.

Beyond that, I'm listing tests for data item retrieval by index and period (including out-of-bounds and not-found cases), index lookups, value retrieval, and the various add/update operations including validation for null items, wrong period classes, duplicates, and max count trimming, plus notification behavior and the add-or-update variants.

I continue outlining tests for aged-item removal with various notify flags and edge cases, clearing the series, deleting periods and ranges (with validation), cloning, and the createCopy methods covering start/end validation, empty data, and period-based range creation.

Then I plan equals() tests covering same instance, null/different class, differing domain, range, max item age/count, item count, and data item, plus a true-equality case, along with hashCode consistency across varying item counts. I'll rely on the Day class from the same package for time periods, importing TimeSeriesDataItem, SeriesException, and the series change listener classes needed for the tests.

I'm sketching out a test listener that flips a flag when a series change event fires, then registering it on the series. I'm also mapping out edge cases like passing null to getIndex expecting an exception, adding a mismatched period type (Year instead of Day) to trigger a class error, adding a duplicate period to trigger a SeriesException, and inserting periods out of order to verify correct sequencing.

Setting up Day instances for the insertion test...

I'm also planning tests for maximum item count enforcement when adding or updating items, and thinking through how removeAgedItems relies on RegularTimePeriod's createInstance method to work correctly across different period types like Day and Year.

This confirms it's a real utility method that constructs the correct time period type from the given class. Now I need to trace how setMaximumItemAge and removeAgedItems interact — setMaximumItemAge(long) calls the boolean-only overload of removeAgedItems, while there's a separate overload taking a latest timestamp plus boolean that I need to check for my test case with Day-based series.

For a minimal test, I'll build a Day series, add items across Jan 1-10 2020, then call the timestamp-based removeAgedItems with a future date and notify=true, checking that all items get purged and the listener fires.

I'll set maximumItemAge to a small number since items dated 2020 versus 'now' will differ by thousands of days regardless. I should also check that calling removeAgedItems on an empty series does nothing and throws no exception, since the while loop condition fails immediately when getItemCount() is 0.

The reflection-based exception branches (NoSuchMethodException, IllegalAccessException, InvocationTargetException) are essentially unreachable without mocking since createInstance exists publicly, so I'll skip testing those and note it in a comment. I still need to verify the "count == 0" branch for adding the first item, test hashCode with three or more items, confirm getKey() works properly through addAndOrUpdate, and import SeriesException for the equals tests.

To test the getClass() mismatch branch in equals(), I'm creating an anonymous subclass of TimeSeries so I can compare a plain TimeSeries against a subclass instance with identical data—since their classes differ, equals() should return false. I also want to cover the branch checking whether the object isn't a TimeSeries or fails super.equals(), so I'll test with both a non-TimeSeries object and a TimeSeries with a different name, assuming Series.equals compares the series key among other properties.

Now I'm assembling the full test suite, being careful that TimeSeriesDataItem, Day, and Year constructors and methods match the actual JFreeChart API. I also want a test confirming that calling getTimePeriod() with an invalid index throws an IndexOutOfBoundsException, since getDataItem delegates to the underlying list's get() method.

Now I'm double-checking the boundary case where setMaximumItemCount(0) is called on empty data—confirming count stays at 0 so no deletion happens and no exception is thrown.

For the trimming test, I trace through the delete logic: with 3 items and maximum set to 2, the delete call removes only index 0, leaving Day2 and Day3 remaining, which matches my assertion.

Then I work through the zero-age boundary case, tracing removeAgedItems with two consecutive days—checking the serial index difference between periods to see if the aging logic correctly flags items for removal.

I trace through the loop mechanics carefully: since latest is computed once before the while loop starts, removing an item doesn't recompute it, so after day1 is removed and getItemCount() drops to 1, the diff between latest and the new getTimePeriod(0) becomes zero, causing the loop to exit properly with day2 remaining as expected.

Now I'm setting up the third test case with a single item to verify no removal happens when there's just one data point.

Then for the fourth test with three items, I trace through: setting maximumItemAge to 1 triggers removeAgedItems, latest is fixed at day3's serial, and the loop removes day1 first since the initial diff exceeds 1, then stops after checking day2 since diff equals exactly 1. I confirm the listener setup order matches so the notification flag gets set correctly since setMaximumItemAge always calls removeAgedItems with notify=true.

Now for the long-variant test, setMaximumItemAge(5) is called first on an empty series, so removeAgedItems is a no-op since there are no items yet. After adding day1 and day2, their internal add() calls trigger removeAgedItems(false) but the diff is too small to remove anything, then the explicit far-future call with notify=true forces removal of both items since the huge time gap exceeds the max age, matching the expected zero count and fired listener.

For the notify-false variant, only a single item is added so the per-add removal check is skipped (needs itemCount>1), but the explicit far-future call still removes the lone item since itemCount>0 and the diff exceeds maxAge - the removal happens but the listener isn't fired since notify is false, matching assertFalse.

Now I'm looking at testEqualsDifferentClass, which uses a TimeSeriesSubclass with only a name constructor to test equality across different classes.

I trace through equals: comparing a plain TimeSeries against the subclass instance passes the instanceof check and superclass field comparison since both share the same name, and domain/range descriptions match by default, but the final getClass() comparison catches that one is TimeSeries.class and the other TimeSeriesSubclass.class, so equals correctly returns false.

Then for testEqualsNullOrDifferentType, I'm checking that series.equals(null) fails the instanceof check since null isn't a TimeSeries.

Now moving on to addAndOrUpdate: I'm noting the series name uses "Overwritten values from: " plus the key, and since this test only checks counts/values not names, that's fine. I'm tracing that Day1 gets overwritten from 1.0 to 100 and Day2=200 gets added as new, since addOrUpdate iterates through the other series' items applying overwrite/insert logic per period.

I'm confirming the timePeriodClass used for the returned "overwritten" series comes from the parameter series (other.getTimePeriodClass()), which matches Day.class as expected since both series use Day periods, so the logic checks out consistently.

The test assertions match up: overwritten should have exactly one item with the original value 1.0, while the main series ends with both days updated correctly. Now I'm moving on to check the createCopy behavior when the series has empty data and start/end indices are 0 and -1.

Wait, I need to reconsider - end<start check would trigger first since -1<0, so my assumed exception for that case is wrong. To actually hit the empty-data branch, I'd need valid start<=end bounds, but calling createCopy(0,0) on empty data would instead throw an IndexOutOfBoundsException when it tries to access the nonexistent index.

Actually, re-examining: the for-loop only executes if data.size()>0, so with an empty series, createCopy(0,0) satisfies start>=0 and end>=start without ever entering the loop, avoiding the index error entirely. I should fix my test to use createCopy(0,0) instead of (0,-1), then verify the resulting copy has an empty item count.

I still need to double-check other cases like negative start, end<start, and a valid range copy across three items to make sure those all throw or return the right results. Now I want to trace through the boundary case where the series has only one item and I request a copy for a period range that starts after the last item, tracking how binarySearch computes the insertion index when the target date isn't present.

Working through this, the negative insertion result correctly converts to an index equal to the data size, which triggers the empty-range branch as expected -- confirming that this boundary case is handled correctly even when the end index computation continues afterward.

Since endIndex is 0 rather than negative, that check doesn't override emptyRange, but it's already true from the start adjustment, so we fall into the empty-copy branch, which matches the test's expectation of a zero-item result. Moving to the next test case: with series containing day1 and day3, calling createCopy(day1, day2) should have start match at index 0 directly.

Since day2 isn't in the series, its insertion point falls between day1 and day3, giving a negative index that resolves to endIndex=0 after adjustment—pointing back to day1. With startIndex and endIndex both 0 and neither triggering the empty-range conditions, the copy includes only day1, giving a count of 1, which lines up with the expected assertion.

Now I want to verify the valid-range test case where all three days are present in the series, so both start and end indices should resolve directly without any insertion-point adjustments.

I'm also checking that the unmodifiable list test correctly blocks additions, that adding a wrong period class type throws the expected SeriesException, and confirming that SeriesException behaves as an unchecked exception so it doesn't require declared throws clauses on the relevant methods.

Now I'm verifying createCopy declares CloneNotSupportedException so test methods calling it need "throws Exception", and checking that deleteRange validates start/end order before checking data size, and that setting maximum item count to zero on empty data correctly reports zero.

I also want to confirm Day equality relies on serial day number comparison, so two Day objects for the same calendar date should be equal, which matters for asserting time period values in the series.

I'm also checking that using a fully-qualified GregorianCalendar reference inline avoids needing an explicit import statement.

System.currentTimeMillis() is fine since System is always available in java.lang, and TimeSeriesDataItem's constructor should be public for direct instantiation. I'm also noting that Series lives in org.jfree.data.general but isn't directly instantiated in the tests.

The addChangeListener(SeriesChangeListener) method is likely inherited from Series and is standard in JFreeChart's API, while fireSeriesChanged() is protected and doesn't need direct test calls since it's triggered indirectly. I believe this test set covers everything needed.

Now I'm finalizing the code with the one bug fix identified for testCreateCopyEmptyData. I'm also verifying edge cases: createCopy(-1,0) throws immediately since start<0 is checked first regardless of end, and createCopy(1,0) throws since end<start, both matching expected behavior in testCreateCopyStartNegativeThrows and testCreateCopyEndLessThanStartThrows.

I'm double-checking that createCopy(0,0) with int literals correctly resolves to the (int,int) overload rather than the RegularTimePeriod version, and confirming testCreateCopyEmptyData now correctly returns a copy with zero items when the series is empty and start=end=0. Now I'm verifying testCloneIndependence, checking that series.clone() returns a properly independent Object.

Now I'm tracing through testAddInsertMiddleItem to confirm binarySearch finds the correct insertion index when day2 is added between day1 and day3, verifying the comparison logic falls into the else branch and computes insertion index 1 as expected.

Then I check testAddDuplicatePeriodThrows: adding day1 twice hits the else branch, binarySearch finds an exact match at index 0, and since that's non-negative it should throw a SeriesException for duplicate periods.

For testAddExceedsMaximumItemCountRemovesFirst, setting maximum to 2 before adding anything does nothing since the list is empty, then adding day1, day2, day3 sequentially causes the third add to push total size to 3, triggering removal of index 0 (day1), leaving the final list as [day2, day3].

Now checking testAddOrUpdateExceedsMaximumItemCount: setting maximum to 1 on an empty series does nothing, then addOrUpdate for day1 inserts it fine since count stays at 1. Adding day2 next inserts it after day1, bringing count to 2 which exceeds the maximum of 1, so index 0 (day1) gets removed, leaving just day2 as the final single-item result.

Everything checks out consistently now, so I'll finalize the corrected code with the fix applied, plus put together a summary table mapping each test to the branches and conditions it covers -- with the table itself in Thai per the request while keeping code comments primarily in English. I'm also considering adding one more test for robustness, checking that calling getTimePeriod on an empty series throws an IndexOutOfBoundsException, though I may skip it if time is tight.

I'll add quick tests for getNextTimePeriod behavior on an empty series expecting the same kind of exception, then double-check that testGetIndexNotFound and testSetDomainDescriptionNull assertions hold up correctly. I also want to flag as a black-box assumption that Series equals/hashCode relies on the key, since getting that wrong could cause unexpected test failures.

I also need to flag the reflection-based catch blocks in removeAgedItems as unreachable via public API, adding a comment rather than fabricating a test for them. Now I'm ready to put together the final answer with the code and explanation.
